title: What changes an asteroid’s path?
target: Explain how gravity can change velocity without contact.
criteria: Draw velocity tangent to a path and force toward the attracting body.
Distinguish motion from a change in motion.
State what a straight-line model leaves out.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: At the top of a circular path, an object moves clockwise. In which direction is its instantaneous velocity?
options: Zero because it is at the top.
cpa.guide: Clockwise motion at the top is tangent to the right.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A satellite is directly east of a spherical planet. Which direction is the planet’s gravitational force on it?
cpa.guide: Gravity is attractive and points toward the source center.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An object maintains a constant speed while turning. Is its velocity changing?
options: No; speed and velocity are identical quantities.
Yes; direction is part of velocity.
Only if it comes to rest.
cpa.guide: Velocity is a vector; a direction change is a velocity change.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A probe initially moves north. A brief eastward force changes its velocity. Which change is caused directly by this force?
options: Instant loss of all northward velocity.
cpa.guide: Acceleration follows net force; an eastward impulse changes the east component.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: What does a constant-velocity straight-line prediction omit when gravity is significant?
options: The change in velocity caused by gravity.
cpa.guide: A nonzero net gravitational force changes velocity from the straight-line estimate.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two predictions for a probe separate over time: one includes gravity, one assumes constant velocity. Which observation would favor including gravity?
options: A measured bending path toward the attracting body.
An unchanged name for the probe.
A constant speed alone, with no direction information.
cpa.guide: Curvature toward the source is evidence of a changing velocity consistent with gravity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.
